title: The Mosso Tree
html:
If you're in New Zealand you might have thought you wouldn't hear from me today. However, I never miss a Monday and, for those of you overseas who don't have a day off today, this is for you.

This weekend I have been thinking about success and how long it takes. Even 'overnight' successes are never that; they were working, studying and practicing long before they appeared to be successful.

Success comes from trial and error, making mistakes, learning from them and moving on. It is a process and there are no short cuts. This is proven by what is going on in the world now. People eager for success have taken short cuts that have come back to bite them very hard and, in some cases, taking others down with them. 

I read that in China there is a giant bamboo called the Mosso tree that, after planting, takes four years to appear above the ground. After that it grows at an amazing rate of one metre per day!

What was it doing under the ground all that time? Growing roots (foundations) and preparing itself for growth.

This week think about the Mosso tree and realise everything you are doing lays the foundations for your 'overnight' success.
